builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CAMP: Context-Aware Mapping and Placement for LLMs on 3D-IMC Arrays
summary: Replaces prior weight-placement heuristics for 3D analog in-memory computing (AIMC) accelerators with a profiling-driven, context-aware mapping that accounts for MVM concurrency conflicts. The cost is an offline profiling and search loop plus a constraint on deploying to specialized 3D-IMC analog hardware; no model retraining is required. It fails outright without access to 3D-IMC chips, and its gains depend on the target architecture and runtime context, so results may not transfer across different AIMC designs or workloads.
rationale: The reader operates on a 24 GB GPU or third-party APIs and has no access to experimental analog in-memory computing hardware, so this technique cannot be adopted or meaningfully tested in their production practice.
technique: Offline weight-mapping algorithm for 3D analog in-memory computing LLM accelerators

claims.statement: Replaces prior weight-placement heuristics for 3D analog in-memory computing (AIMC) accelerators with a profiling-driven, context-aware mapping that accounts for MVM concurrency conflicts. The cost is an offline profiling and search loop plus a constraint on deploying to specialized 3D-IMC analog hardware; no model retraining is required. It fails outright without access to 3D-IMC chips, and its gains depend on the target architecture and runtime context, so results may not transfer across different AIMC designs or workloads.
Up to 2.0x higher 3D-IMC throughput and 1.74x higher end-to-end throughput over state-of-the-art mapping algorithms; compute utilization improved from 42.4% to 60.3%.
